column1: # PRESET OVERRIDE FRONTIER — every place a resolved preset value can be
# replaced before the lane that consumes it reads it.
# Columns:  file <TAB> field <TAB> count <TAB> class <TAB> note
# The DELIVERY SURFACE is derived from source: every `config.<field> = ...` in
# `crates/ny-cli/src/preset/apply.rs`, which is the one place a shipped yaml key
# lands. A write to any of those fields ANYWHERE ELSE in first-party non-test
# code is an override site and must appear below. A `<Type>::default` row is the
# blast-radius version: a whole resolved config rebuilt from scratch, dropping
#   runtime-clear      REPLACES an armed value during a run. The dangerous
#                      class. The note MUST carry a `when=` clause naming the
#   config-rebuild     rebuilds a whole resolved config from `::default()`.
#   derived-scope      derives a scoped sub-solve config from the parent's
#                      resolved value (a narrowed slice, a per-clause budget).
#   derived-value      writes a value computed FROM the preset value, or fills a
#                      field the preset left unset. Preset-preserving.
#   legacy-unreviewed  measured and not yet adjudicated. Capped by
#                      BASELINE_LEGACY_UNREVIEWED; a NEW site can never land
#                      here, because an undeclared identity fails first.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `configs/vnncomp25/cgan_2023.yaml` has said
# `bab.clip.relaxed: true` for its whole life, and six shipped cgan presets say
# it. It has never once been true at the lane: a BatchNorm makes the graph
# `config_with_disjunctive_clip_routes_disabled` zeroes the field on a clone of
# the resolved config. There is no telemetry for that clear. Nothing in the
# config, the log, or either existing ratchet could have told you.
# A row here is a RECEIPT, not an endorsement. Additions and removals BOTH fail,
# so removing a site is a deliberate edit in the same commit — and so is adding
# one, which is the whole point.
# READ THE ROW BEFORE MEASURING THROUGH A KEY. A null taken through a
# `runtime-clear` whose guard your benchmark hits is VOID, not negative.

It fires ONLY when the router ACTS (router.mode: on, declaration default off, no shipped yaml sets it) and the rule's own router.rules.* switch is on; it never touches a key the row's configuration pinned (VerifierPins: bab.{max_depth,disjunctive_clause_retry_passes,initial_bounds_warmup_fallback}.is_some() => blocked_by=pin, value unchanged) and never lowers the value in force (max). Every application prints `[router] derived rule= key= from= to= source=router [blocked_by=]`. Value: one pass per second of the plan's prover window (router::derive::clause_passes), the loop still stopping when a pass decides nothing and never eating the Graph-MIP-reserving bab_deadline.

#router-r5 CR-RS (router::route::apply_config_settings via apply_to_verifier_config), called once at the verifier's configuration boundary right after CR-K's apply_verifier_directives. It fires ONLY when the router ACTS (router.mode: on, declaration default off, no shipped yaml sets it), router.rules.route is on AND the route authority holds a route for the capability, which the pure commit grants only at SR.seal (S7 + S8 done on its recorded envelope) with the row's facts inside that envelope and NO route key pinned by the row (its file under any path the key is written at — solver.alpha_crown.* and its bab.alpha_crown.* twin — or a non-default lever source => pin:<key>, never routed; a pin on a sealed capability is pin debt). So it never replaces a value the yaml asked for: it fills a key the yaml left unset with the value the capability's own sealed evidence arm ran, copying the resolved field and changing ONLY `enabled` (max_generators / max_secs keep the row's values).
